evidence: The study's own codebook states the pairing item by item, which is what makes this VERIFIED rather than inferred: Codebook.xlsx sheet "Study 1" carries one row per it.* variable holding that variable's own item text, subscale and response scale, so every item is distinguished from every other by the source itself, not by position. The live code is that variable name with dots stripped and lowercased -- study1-maindat.csv's header is literally 'it.MCQ.F1', Stata's import delimited drops the dots (illegal in a Stata name) and data/sun_2025_morality.do then does `rename *, lower`. Deterministic, one-to-one, no reordering. Item sets match at 4 items and resp sets match. CORROBORATION on the shipped wording, from keying polarity: itmcqf3 is the odd-signed item and the data agrees -- M = 1.49 against 4.45-4.57 for the other three, mean r = -0.420. SUPERSEDES this table's earlier PARTIAL row, which was testing a substitution (normdat-labels.csv's `mv.*` fragments standing in for the `it.*` items) that should never have been made; the correct source needs no substitution.

The three questions are reproduced verbatim in the S1 File's 'Part 4 : Additional questions' block, and verify_shu_2025_translation_add.R re-checks each shipped item_text against that cached file rather than re-checking counts. Two codes are pinned by content match. The third, addcompetitioninreha, rests on elimination alone: its code reads 'competition' where the remaining question concerns study pressure and career plans. No data-side route exists to separate the three -- the article publishes no per-item statistics and the items share no structure a statistic could distinguish -- and the one asymmetry that might have helped, addcompetitioninreha using resp 1-4 against 1-5 for the other two, cannot be used because the S1 File states no response options for any of them. Hence PARTIAL on 2 of 3 items pinned.

Nothing to check: the Oxford ARC data paper's own processed_data_dictionary.csv keys every item code here to its Field_Label verbatim, and the codes are self-describing besides (media_why_tv_news), so no order or position was inferred at any point. validate_items.R was run against the 44-item live table and reported item and resp sets matching (44 items, 179,937 rows). The file has since been cut to the 36 'radio' items (180 rows) because the 8 hours-per-day items are being dropped from the response table -- see #1996 and PR #2008. UPLOAD ORDER: this item table must go up only AFTER #2008 is merged and oxfordcovid_xue_2024_at is re-uploaded at 36 items / 136,467 rows; uploading it before that would leave the item and resp sets disagreeing with live data. audit_batch.R's WARN on the 44-item version is the instrument's conditional structure, not a defect: the 36 reason items fall into six clusters of six with near-identical n inside each cluster (2,264-2,304, 2,410-2,465, 2,883-2,955, 4,201-4,242, 4,301-4,545, 6,193-6,277), because each medium's six reasons were asked only of respondents who used that medium. The same WARN's blank-option_text half was the hours-per-day items and is resolved by their removal.

Three routes. (1) The published DERS-36 numbering is the 41-item pool minus items 2, 11, 13, 18, 36, renumbered ascending; under that rule Table III's 11 reverse-scored items land on exactly positions 1, 2, 6, 7, 8, 10, 17, 20, 22, 24, 34. (2) Those same 11 positions are pinned independently by the deposit: dropping DERS_37_POST and reversing them reproduces DERS_SUM_POST for 90 of 90 complete rows, against a best-of-36 alternative drop of 42 of 90 and 6 of 90 for no reverses -- which also shows the items are stored raw and that column 37 is unscored. (3) Grouping the 36 columns by Table III's six factors gives mean within-subscale r = 0.503, above the maximum (0.440) of 2000 same-sized random groupings, p = 0.0005, so each item is pinned to its subscale. LIMIT, and the reason this is PARTIAL not VERIFIED: routes 1-2 fix polarity class and the unscored column, route 3 fixes subscale membership, but two items sharing a subscale and a polarity are still interchangeable on the evidence. Their individual assignment rests on the monotone renumbering rather than on the data. A rival ordering that preserved both polarity and subscale would not be detected.

Exempt: there is no mapping step to verify. The .sav variable label sits on the very column that becomes the item code -- NFC_1's label is the text shipped for nfc_1 -- and data/pezzuti_2025_coolpeople.do reaches the live code by `rename *, lower` followed by `gen item = "`var'"`, with no reordering, renumbering or positional assignment anywhere in the block (lines 1023-1066). Item sets match exactly at 5 items and resp sets match exactly at 1-7. The one thing the source does NOT settle is which published instrument this is; that is recorded in provenance as an identification from the article's citation of Yoo et al. (2011) plus a wording match, and it has no bearing on the code-to-text mapping.

Exempt, and stronger than the usual data_labels exemption. The .sav variable label sits on the very column that becomes the item code, AND the label states the item's own number, so the source asserts the code-to-text pairing instead of leaving it to position: the parsed leading numbers are exactly 1..11 against PBA1..PBA11. Both studies' label sets were parsed separately and are identical on all 11 wordings. data/singh_2025_identity.do reaches the live code by `rename *, lower` with no reordering. Independent confirmation: the CC-BY article reproduces one sample item and it matches shipped pba3 verbatim. Item sets match at 11 items, resp sets at 1-5. What is NOT settled by the source is the midpoint anchor for the pooled table, since the two administrations worded it differently and only one row per (item, resp) can exist; that is disclosed in provenance rather than verified.

Three routes, all re-runnable in verify_socialstereotype_hughes_2025_judgement.R. (1) The codebook reports credibility of the person as the mean of 'I believe this person's story' and reversed 'I think I got an incomplete or inaccurate story', M = 4.59, SD = 0.71. Across all 12 ordered pairs of ce1/ce2/ce4/ce5 only ce1 with reversed ce2 reproduces it (M = 4.59, SD = 0.70); the reverse orientation gives M = 1.41 and no other pair is within 0.4 of the target mean. Reported alpha .66 vs observed .72 is the one discrepancy. (2) nps ('how likely would you recommend the product or company') separates the two remaining codes by sign: r(ce4, nps) = +0.447, r(ce5, nps) = -0.572, so ce4 is the patronize item and ce5 the avoid item; item means agree (2.48 vs 3.42, in a complaint context). (3) The codebook calls Interest in Affiliation a FIVE-item scale with M = 3.98, SD = 0.87, alpha = .93 while the live table has six affil codes; dropping affil6 yields alpha = .932, M = 3.97, SD = 0.87, the best of all six drops (next best alpha .910), and affil6 has the lowest mean inter-item r (0.495 vs 0.656-0.725). NOT ESTABLISHED, and the reason this is PARTIAL: the individual wording of affil1-affil5. The codebook gives two unkeyed examples for five items, so those five plus affil6 ship with empty item_text. Six of the twelve items have verified wording; six have none. Nothing here distinguishes affil2 from affil3. ROUTE 4, now the primary evidence for the affil6 finding and stronger than route 3: the deposit's 'SES stereotypes_scored data.csv' ships affil1-affil6 next to the authors' own scored `affil` composite. Averaging the five items with affil6 dropped reproduces that composite exactly for all 1,211 complete rows; averaging all six matches 221, and no other single-item drop exceeds 565. This is the authors' scoring reproduced, not inferred from reliability. The wording search is also closed: the full deposit was enumerated and the preregistration gives no affiliation item wording at all, so the codebook's two unkeyed examples are the only wording in the record and affil1-affil6 remain blank. Still PARTIAL for exactly that reason. ROUTE 5, a FAILED route recorded because the failure is the finding: the five affiliation wordings are now known from Tackman & Srivastava (2016) but cannot be keyed to affil1-affil5. Item means support (a) at affil1 (highest, 4.297) and (e) at affil5 (lowest, 3.395), but the middle three are open, and the one discriminating test runs against article order: (d) and (e) share a stem, so (d) should correlate more with (e), yet r(affil3, affil5) = 0.777 > r(affil4, affil5) = 0.723. That is confounded with difficulty (affil3's mean is nearer affil5's), so it settles nothing either way; trait correlations separate affil3 from affil4 by <= 0.02. item_text therefore stays empty for all six affil codes and the wordings live in provenance. Closing this needs the administered Qualtrics form, absent from the deposit.
